key_insight: A PICNN trained on finite-volume residuals can serve as the prediction step in a physics-preserving scheme for two-phase porous-media flow while maintaining thermodynamic consistency through correction.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical surrogate for traditional solvers that better handles local flux physics, discontinuous permeability, and conservation constraints in reservoir and subsurface flow simulations.
method: Use a physics-informed CNN to predict the flow state from finite-volume residuals.
Compute interfacial fluxes with TPFA and two-point difference quotients of neighboring cell-centered values.
Apply post-processing to enforce energy stability, mass conservation, and solution bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing that the finite-volume-residual-trained PICNN can replace the conventional prediction solver and outperform standard PINNs in capturing local interactions.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate residual formulation and correction, so implementation must carefully preserve flux continuity and stability across heterogeneous media.
paper_title: The PICNN-Assisted Physics-Preserving Scheme for Thermodynamically Consistent Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media
